overview/flow.code:
flowchart LR
    CH[ClinicHub] -->|orders, cancels| HUB
    LF[LabFlow] -->|results| HUB
    CR[ClinicReport] -->|results| HUB
    CH & LF & CR & PF[PharmaFlow] -->|financial documents| HUB
    HUB[IntegrationHub] --> CH & LF & CR & FIN[FinancePowerApp]
    HUB -->|de-identified events| MQ[(RabbitMQ)] --> AN[Analytics]
    EXT[External lab / OLIS sim] <-->|HL7 v2 over MLLP| HUB
    HUB --- DB[(PostgreSQL: message log)]

overview/decisions.code:
1. **A relay first, not a new owner.** ClinicHub owns patients and orders; LabFlow and ClinicReport own results;
   FinancePowerApp owns the books. The hub owns only its message log and its routes.
2. **Synchronous routes stay synchronous.** ClinicHub stores the ids from the transaction-response, and a `409` on a
   cancel is an answer. The hub returns the upstream's status and body unchanged, `502` if the upstream refused the
   connection, `504` on timeout. It does not retry: the senders' outboxes already do.
3. **The sender's token goes through.** The hub validates it (ClinicHub's JWKS, issuer, expiry, an audience and scope
   allowed on that route) and forwards the same `Authorization` header, so each receiver's own checks — "a result only
   from the app the order went to" — keep working. The hub never signs on behalf of another application.
4. **No health information in the log by default.** The log records metadata: route, sender (client id), clinic,
   resource types and counts, Bundle id, identifiers of ServiceRequests/DiagnosticReports, status, latency, size, a
   SHA-256 of the body. Storing bodies is a setting (`hub.payloads.store`), off by default; when on, bodies are
   encrypted (AES-GCM, key from configuration), kept for `hub.payloads.retentionDays` (default 30), and every view of
   a body is written to an access log (PHIPA).
5. **Asynchronous only where the outside world is asynchronous:** HL7 v2 (MLLP, ACKs) and the event feed to Analytics.

relay/refuse.code:
private void refuse(
    HttpServletResponse response,
    CallContext call,
    long started,
    int status,
    String code,
    String text,
    String reason)
    throws IOException {
  response.setStatus(status);
  response.setContentType("application/fhir+json");
  response
      .getOutputStream()
      .write(
          ("{\"resourceType\":\"OperationOutcome\",\"issue\":[{\"severity\":\"error\",\"code\":\""
                  + code
                  + "\",\"diagnostics\":\""
                  + text
                  + "\"}]}")
              .getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
  finish(call, started, null, status, status + " " + reason);

tokens/decoder.code:
decoder =
    NimbusJwtDecoder.withJwkSetUri(properties.auth().effectiveJwksUri())
        .jwsAlgorithm(SignatureAlgorithm.RS256)
        // OpenIddict marks access tokens "at+jwt" (RFC 9068); the default accepts only "JWT".
        .jwtProcessorCustomizer(
            processor ->
                processor.setJWSTypeVerifier(
                    new DefaultJOSEObjectTypeVerifier<SecurityContext>(
                        JOSEObjectType.JWT, new JOSEObjectType("at+jwt"), null)))
        .build();
decoder.setJwtValidator(JwtValidators.createDefaultWithIssuer(properties.auth().issuer()));

forward/yml.code:
# The cancel is PUT .../ServiceRequest?identifier=system|42. Tomcat refuses a raw | (and these)
# in a query by default; the relay percent-encodes them when it forwards.
relaxed-query-chars: '|,{,},[,],^,<,>,",`,\'

message-log/schema.code:
CREATE TABLE message (
    id               uuid         PRIMARY KEY,
    received_at      timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    route            varchar(60)  NOT NULL,
    direction        varchar(10)  NOT NULL CHECK (direction IN ('inbound', 'outbound')),
    sender_client_id varchar(100),
    clinic_slug      varchar(60),
    method           varchar(10)  NOT NULL,
    path             text         NOT NULL,
    content_type     varchar(200),
    request_size     bigint,
    request_sha256   char(64),
    bundle_id        varchar(100),
    resource_summary jsonb,
    upstream_status  integer,
    latency_ms       integer,
    error            text
);

CREATE INDEX ix_message_received_at ON message (received_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX ix_message_route_status ON message (route, upstream_status);
CREATE INDEX ix_message_clinic ON message (clinic_slug, received_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX ix_message_bundle ON message (bundle_id);

event-factory/types.code:
* Turns one relayed call into zero or more events. Events are about answers: a call the upstream * did not answer (unreachable, timeout) makes none, so the sender's retry makes them once. * *
    *
  • {@code order.placed}: an order Bundle the upstream answered, whatever the answer. *
  • {@code order.accepted}: the same, answered 2xx. *
  • {@code order.cancelled} / {@code order.cancel-refused}: a cancel answered 2xx / 409. *
  • {@code result.final} / {@code result.amended}: a DiagnosticReport in that status, answered * 2xx. Other statuses make no event. *
  • {@code finance.document}: each financial document of a call answered 2xx. *
* * Prescriptions and patient merges make no event (a drug says too much about a patient). A merge * answered 2xx moves the pseudonym remembered with the merged patient's orders to the survivor's, * so later results of those orders carry the survivor's pseudonym. * *

Event ids are derived from the content, so the same call sent twice is one event.

pseudonym/link.code:
-- What a later call needs to know about an order: results and cancels do not carry the patient, so the
-- pseudonym, test and priority are remembered from the order. De-identified: no MRN, no name.
CREATE TABLE order_link (
    clinic_slug       varchar(60)  NOT NULL,
    order_id          varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    patient_pseudonym char(64),
    application       varchar(60),
    test_code_system  varchar(200),
    test_code         varchar(100),
    priority          varchar(20),
    created_at        timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (clinic_slug, order_id)

pseudonym/upsert.code:
on conflict (clinic_slug, order_id) do update set
  patient_pseudonym = coalesce(excluded.patient_pseudonym, order_link.patient_pseudonym),
  application = coalesce(excluded.application, order_link.application),
  test_code_system = coalesce(excluded.test_code_system, order_link.test_code_system),
  test_code = coalesce(excluded.test_code, order_link.test_code),
  priority = coalesce(excluded.priority, order_link.priority)

outbox/table.code:
CREATE TABLE event_outbox (
    id              uuid         PRIMARY KEY,
    message_id      uuid,
    created_at      timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    event_type      varchar(60)  NOT NULL,
    payload         jsonb        NOT NULL,
    attempts        integer      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    next_attempt_at timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    published_at    timestamptz,
    last_error      varchar(200)

outbox/publish.code:
select id, event_type, payload::text, attempts from event_outbox
 where published_at is null and next_attempt_at <= now()
 order by created_at limit ? for update skip locked

oru/table.code:
| HL7 v2 | FHIR R4 |
|---|---|
| MSH-3.MSH-4, MSH-10 | sender id (`EXTLAB.LAB1`) and message id, used for de-duplication; Bundle id and resource ids are derived from them, so a resend gives the same ids |
| ORC-2 / OBR-2 placer order number `101^harbourview` (or the whole `urn:clinichub:harbourview:service-request` as the first component) | `DiagnosticReport.basedOn.identifier` = `urn:clinichub:harbourview:service-request\|101` |
| ORC-3 / OBR-3 filler order number | `DiagnosticReport.identifier` (`urn:integrationhub:hl7:{sender}:filler-order`) |
| OBR-4 | `DiagnosticReport.code` (LN → LOINC, SCT → SNOMED, an unknown system name → `urn:integrationhub:hl7:{sender}:{name}`) |
| OBR-7 / OBR-22 | `effectiveDateTime` / `issued` |
| OBR-25 (table 0123) | `status`: F final, C amended, X cancelled; P, R, A, O, I, S, Y are accepted and **not forwarded** (ClinicHub takes final, amended, cancelled) |
| OBX-2 NM / SN / ST, TX, FT / CE, CWE, CNE | `valueQuantity` (with `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` as comparator, unit from OBX-6 as UCUM) / `valueString` / `valueCodeableConcept` |
| OBX-3 | `Observation.code`; the Observations are `DiagnosticReport.result` |
| OBX-7 | `referenceRange` (text, and low/high when it is `a-b`, `<a` or `>a`) |
| OBX-8 (table 0078, repeating) | `interpretation` (v3 ObservationInterpretation); a flag not in the table is kept as text |
| OBX-11 (table 0085) | `Observation.status`; OBX-14, else OBR-7 → `effectiveDateTime` |
| NTE after an OBX / after the OBR | `Observation.note` / `DiagnosticReport.conclusion` |
| PID, PV1, NK1, … | **not read**. No patient is named in what goes to ClinicHub; it knows the patient from the order |

store-forward/insert.code:
insert into hl7_inbound (id, received_at, sender, control_id, status, report_count, next_attempt_at, payload)
values (?, ?, ?, ?, 'PENDING', ?, now() + make_interval(secs => ?), ?)
on conflict (sender, control_id) do update
   set status = 'PENDING', attempts = 0, received_at = excluded.received_at,
       next_attempt_at = excluded.next_attempt_at, payload = excluded.payload,
       report_count = excluded.report_count, last_error = null, last_status = null, id = excluded.id
 where hl7_inbound.status in ('FAILED', 'REJECTED')

orders-out/send.code:
* A route for an external laboratory: the order Bundle is sent as an ORM^O01 and the lab's ACK is
* the answer. 200 when the lab took it; 409 for a cancellation and 422 for an order the lab
* refused (ClinicHub treats 409 as an answer and 422 as a failure to retry); 502 when the lab did
* not answer; 503 when no lab is set up; 400 when the body cannot be an order.
*/
